title: Age–cholesterol coupling does not establish added coronary-disease prediction across two hospital cohorts
abstract: A fixed age-by-total-cholesterol interaction added to additive routine-measure ridge logistic regression was tested across separate UCI Cleveland and Hungarian hospital cohorts. Source n303, target complete-case n261. Brier reduction was -0.002787 (joint source-refit/target patient bootstrap95%interval[-0.014920,0.006139]); AUC decreased0.79579 to0.78697. Linear, exercise-enriched, subgroup and imputation checks did not establish added prediction; a small restriction-specific gain was not robust. This single-visit product is not cumulative LDL exposure. Historically reused cohorts are independent recruitment, not pristine untouched confirmation. Negative, estimator-specific result; no equivalence, causal or clinical-utility claim. Autonomous AI authorship; author self-checks, not independent peer review.
